s: Which of the following is not part of recommendations of Rajmannar Committee?
o: No decision of national importance or which may affect one or more states should be taken by the Union government except after consultation with the Inter state council
Every bill of national importance or which may affect one or more states should before its introduction in parliament be referred to the Inter state council.
Article 356 should be used only in the event of complete break down of law and order in a state.
Committee recommended vesting of residuary power of legislation and taxation in the state legislature
x:
Laxmikanth: Rajamannar wanted Arts 356, 357 and 365 omitted, so option C is the odd one out. Some guides (gktoday.in) list 'use Art. 356 only in a complete breakdown of law and order' as its recommendation – on that reading every printed option is a recommendation. All sources agree it recommended residuary powers for the States (the printed key).
The Rajamannar Committee (TN, 1969-71) wanted an Inter-State Council set up at once, with Bills and decisions of national importance referred to it, and residuary powers of legislation and taxation vested in the States. On President's Rule Laxmikanth records that it wanted Arts 356, 357 and 365 totally omitted – so 'use Art. 356 only in complete breakdown' is not its recommendation (that line is close to Sarkaria's 'sparingly, as a last resort'). The printed key (residuary powers to States) was in fact one of its recommendations.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about NITI Aayog?

a. NITI Aayog was introduced by Government of India in 2014

b. Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog is appointed by the President of India

c. It has a Governing Council comprising of the Chief Ministers of all the States and Lt. Governors of the Union Territories

d. Regional Councils of NITI Aayog are formed for specified tenure
x: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 (not 2014) and its Vice-Chairperson is appointed by the PM (not the President); its Governing Council has CMs and Lt Governors and Regional Councils are formed for a specified tenure – c and d.

src: APPSC AEE's Screening Test 2019
s: What is the time frame in which the GST Council was to be constituted after commencement of Article 279A of the Constitution?
x: Section 12 of the 101st Amendment Act, 2016 required the President to constitute the GST Council within 60 days of Article 279A coming into force (Council set up 15 Sep 2016).

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The State Finance Commission is constituted under which article of the Constitution?
x: Art. 243I provides for the State Finance Commission for Panchayats. 243H is the Panchayats' taxing power, 243D reservation of seats and 243J audit of accounts.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers 2004
s: The State Finance Commission is appointed by the
x: The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission under Art. 243I every five years; the President appoints the Union Finance Commission (Art. 280).

src: UPSC CSE Prelims 2010
s: Which one of the following authorities makes a recommendation to the Governor of a State as to the principles for determining the taxes and duties which may be appropriated by the Panchayats in that particular State?
o: Panchayati Raj Ministry of that State
x: The State Finance Commission (Art. 243I) recommends to the Governor the principles for determining the taxes, duties, tolls and fees that may be assigned to or appropriated by the Panchayats. District planning bodies and State ministries have no such constitutional role.

src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2010
s: Which one of the following authorities recommends to the Governor about the principles of determination of taxes and fees which may be appropriated by the Panchayats of that state?
x: The State Finance Commission (Art. 243I) recommends to the Governor the principles for determining the taxes, duties, tolls and fees that may be assigned to or appropriated by the Panchayats. District planning bodies and State ministries have no such constitutional role.

src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) (Re. Exam) 2015
s:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer from the code given below:
Assertion (A): State Finance Commission is a Constitutional body.
Reason (R) : Union Finance Commission cannot recommend financial assistance to Panchayats.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: A is true: the SFC is a constitutional body under Art. 243I. R is false: under Art. 280(3)(bb) the Union Finance Commission does recommend measures to augment State funds for Panchayats.

src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2015
s: Which one of the following statements about a State Finance Commission is true?
x: The State Finance Commission is a constitutional body, constituted by the Governor under Art. 243I (73rd Amendment).

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
s: Under the 73rd Amendment, a State Finance Commission is to be set up every?
x: Under Art. 243I the Governor constitutes a State Finance Commission every five years.

src: State PSC
s: To review the financial position of Panchayats, the State Government constitutes every five years a/an
x: Every five years the State (through the Governor) constitutes a Finance Commission under Art. 243I to review the financial position of the Panchayats. It is a commission, not a committee or advisory body.

src: State PSC
s: Who is empowered to review financial position of the Panchayats?
o: Finance Commission constituted by the Governor
x: Under Art. 243I the Finance Commission constituted by the Governor reviews the financial position of the Panchayats.

src: U.P.P.C.S.(Pre) 2013
s: Who amongst the following is responsible for revenue distribution between the State Government and the Local Governments?
x: The State Finance Commission (Art. 243I) recommends the distribution of State taxes, duties, tolls and fees between the State and its local governments; the Governor only acts on its report.

src: APPSC Group-I 1999
s: The State Finance Commission is appointed by
x: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor (i.e. the State Government) every five years under Art. 243I.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: The recommendations of the State Finance Commission are
o: Not binding on the State Government
Binding on the State Government with regard to formula of devolution
Binding on the State Government of Panchayat Raj Schemes
x: The State Finance Commission (Art. 243-I) only recommends; the Governor lays its report with an action-taken memorandum and the State government is not bound by it.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: Third State Finance Commission of AP submitted its report in?
x: The Third State Finance Commission of AP is keyed as reporting in 2008.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The fourteenth finance commission recommended that after credit of grants into account of State Government, if they are not released to panchayats within the following period, state Government would pay interest out of its own funds?
x: The 14th FC asked States to release its grants to the local bodies within 15 days of credit to the State's account; for any delay the State pays interest from its own funds. (The 15th FC later set 10 working days.)

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The fourteenth finance commission recommended that the Central grants?
o: Shall be shared between all levels of local bodies in fixed percentage
Shall directly go to Panchayats only
State Government will decide the shares of local bodies
SFC will decide the shares of local bodies
x: The 14th FC gave its rural grant only to duly constituted Gram Panchayats, which deliver basic services, with no share for block or district Panchayats; it did not leave the split to the States or the SFC.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II 2017
s: With regard to areas under Schedule VI of the Constitution, the grants to local bodies are?
o: Covered by the Central Finance Commission
Not Covered by the Central Finance Commission
There is dispute on this matter
x: Coverage of Sixth Schedule areas has varied: the 13th FC gave a special area grant to areas outside Parts IX/IXA, the 14th FC gave them no local-body grant (the Centre gave one-time special assistance), and the 15th FC again covered Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and traditional bodies.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The fourteenth finance commission recommended devolution of grants to panchayat institutions with population: Area in the weights ratio of?
x: The 14th FC distributed grants for local bodies among the States using 2011 population with 90% weight and area with 10% weight.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The concept of basic grant and performance grant for Panchayats was introduced by?
x: The 13th FC (2010-15) first split local-body grants into a general basic grant and a general performance grant; the 14th FC continued the basic/performance design.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: With regard to trust on local bodies, the 14th Finance Commission held that?
o: There is need to trust and have respect for local bodies
Strict control may be maintained on local bodies as they cannot be trusted
State Governments need not trust the local bodies
No comments are made by the Commission
x: The 14th FC held that local bodies need to be trusted and respected as institutions of self-government, and kept conditions on its grants minimal.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: As per recommendations of Fourteenth Finance Commission, any performance grant of gram panchayats that remains undisbursed would be?
o: Distributed on equitable basis amongst all eligible gram panchayats
Rolled over to next year and then distributed amongst others
Rolled over till end of the 5 year period
No recommendation is made in this regard
x: Under the 14th FC rules, any performance grant left after disbursement to eligible GPs is distributed on an equitable basis among all the eligible Gram Panchayats; it is not rolled over.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: What are the weights to population and area of a State applied by the 14th Finance Commission for distribution of grants?
x: The 14th FC used 2011 population (90%) and area (10%) to distribute local-body grants among the States.

src: APPSC Group-II Prelims 2017 (26-02-2017)
s: As per the recommendations of the 14th Finance Commission, the proportion of basic grant and performance grant out of the total grant to a duly constituted Panchayat would be in the ratio of
x: The 14th FC fixed the basic:performance ratio at 90:10 for Gram Panchayats; 80:20 is the municipal ratio.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: As advised by Central Government, the Operations & Maintenance cost of Gram Panchayat shall not exceed?
x: Key as printed: Central guidelines (14th FC grants) let a Gram Panchayat spend up to 10% of the allocation on O&M/administrative costs.

src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
s: Every gram panchayat may also levy a duty in the form of a surcharge on the ____ collected by Government on materials other than minerals and minor minerals quarried in the village.
x: Under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994 a Gram Panchayat may levy a surcharge on the seigniorage fee collected by Government on materials (other than minerals and minor minerals) quarried in the village.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test GS-MA 201
s: What is the collected in view of sale and purchase of fixed assets in a Gram Panchayat area and what percentage of amount from the above would be credited to the account of the Gram Panchayat on quarterly basis?
x: Transfer duty, a surcharge on stamp duty on the sale or transfer of immovable property in the GP area (1.5% in AP; printed '1-5'), is collected by the State and credited to the Gram Panchayat. Entertainment tax, mineral cess and profession tax are not levied on property transactions.

src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Assistant Telugu Translator 2019
s: Property tax is a
x: Property (house) tax is a local tax – the major own-source revenue of Panchayats and municipalities.

src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
s: Land cess and registration surcharge
at: Collected by State Government and share is transferred to Gram Panchayat
x: Land cess and the surcharge on stamp duty (registration) are collected by the State Government and the share is transferred to the Gram Panchayats under the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.

src: U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011
s:
Consider the following statements and select the correct answer using the code given below:
Assertion (A) : The Union Finance Commission does not have any role in considering measures for providing financial assistance to local bodies.
Reason (R) : In spite of the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, local government continues to be a state subject in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: A is false: under Art. 280(3)(bb) and (c) the Union Finance Commission recommends measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund for Panchayats and Municipalities, based on the SFC's recommendations. R is true: local government is still a State subject (Entry 5, State List).

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: With regard to measures for augmenting Consolidated Funds of States for Panchayats, how many best practices were enlisted by the 12th Finance Commission?
x: Printed key: the 12th Finance Commission listed 14 best practices for augmenting States' Consolidated Funds for Panchayats. Off-topic here (local-body finance).

src: UPSC CSE Prelims 2023
s:
Consider the following:
1. Demographic performance
2. Forest and ecology
3. Governance reforms
4. Stable government
5. Tax and fiscal efforts For the horizontal tax devolution, the Fifteenth Finance Commission used how many of the above as criteria other than population area and income distance?
x: Besides population, area and income distance, the 15th FC used only three criteria: demographic performance (12.5%), forest and ecology (10%) and tax and fiscal effort (2.5%). Governance reforms and stable government were not criteria.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: Who is the primary auditor for audit of Panchayat Raj Institutions?
x: In AP the Director of State Audit (State Audit Dept, under the AP State Audit Act, 1989) is the primary auditor of PRIs; the CAG only gives technical guidance and support.

src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
s: Which state got the Incremental Devolution Index Award for 2015-16 for empowerment of Village Panchayats?
x: Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim and Odisha were the top performers in the Incremental Devolution Index 2015-16 and shared the award on National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April 2016.

src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
s: The percentage of weightage given to the systems that support for decentralization of PRIs in Devolution Index is
x: In the TISS Devolution Index (2015-16), 'support systems for devolution' (capacity building, constitutional mechanisms, accountability) carries 10% and the operational core (functions, finances, functionaries, autonomy) 90%.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The Panchayat Raj Devolution Index is developed to measure the?
o: Actual devolution of funds and functions
Expected devolution of funds and functions
x: The Devolution Index measures the actual devolution of functions and funds (with functionaries) to Panchayats, in policy and in practice – not merely expected devolution or funds alone.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: Which Panchayat Raj award was received by AP Government from Prime Minister in April, 2016?
x: On National Panchayati Raj Day (24 April 2016) the Prime Minister gave AP the Incremental Devolution Index Award.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following reports is commissioned by the Central Government to assess the policy and legislative framework and outcomes of the States in respect of Panchayati Raj?
x: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj commissions the annual Devolution Index Report ('Status of Devolution to Panchayats in States') to assess States' policy and legislative framework and its outcomes.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The responsibility of preparing devolution report based on devolution index for panchayat raj for the year 2015-16 was entrusted to?
x: The Devolution Report 2015-16 was prepared for the Ministry of Panchayati Raj by the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), which also did 2014-15; IIPA did other editions.

src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
s: The state capacity building institute in AP in the areas of rural development and panchayat raj is:
x: The AP State Institute of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj (APSIRD & PR) is the State's training and capacity-building institute; NIRDPR is the national one.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: Where is the National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj located?
x: The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR) is at Rajendranagar, Hyderabad.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: The mechanism of Ombudsman for local bodies is taken care in AP by entrusting the said function to?
x: In Andhra Pradesh the ombudsman function for local bodies is entrusted to the Lokayukta; banking/insurance ombudsmen and the CAG have no such role.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
s: With regard to maintenance of accounts by Panchayat Raj Institutions, one of the major problems is that?
o: The yearly accounts are not closed within time
Panchayats want specialized agency to manage their accounts
x: The commonly reported problem in panchayat accounts is that yearly accounts are not closed in time (CAG/MoPR studies).

src: APPSC Research Assistants

x: The Expert Committee on Leveraging Panchayats for Efficient Delivery of Public Goods and Services (report 2013) was chaired by Mani Shankar Aiyar.
